## What it is

Penpot is a design and prototyping tool in the browser, like Figma, that saves designs as open formats (SVG, CSS, HTML) and lets designers and developers work on the same files ([penpot/penpot](https://github.com/penpot/penpot)).

**Licence:** `MPL-2.0` (GitHub licence API). The gate's licence table classes it **L1** (research 13 §4); `apps/_intake/CANDIDATES.md` lists it as L2 because its brief put MPL under copyleft, which changes no tier. There is no license-matrix row yet, so the gate notes that it is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10).

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): developer: design. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`), five containers in one pod: `frontend` (nginx, the app), `backend` (Java), `exporter` (headless Chromium for PDF and image exports), and native sidecars `db` (PostgreSQL 15, as upstream's compose file) and `valkey` (Valkey 8.1, capped at 128 MB as upstream recommends). They talk over 127.0.0.1; the database and Valkey listen on 127.0.0.1 only, and PostgreSQL trusts local connections, so there is no database password and no Secret.
- `PENPOT_SECRET_KEY` is generated once by an init container onto the data volume, outside the assets folder the frontend serves, and loaded by the backend and exporter commands before the images' own commands run.
- Flags: `disable-email-verification` (no mail server is packaged), `disable-secure-session-cookies` (the app is reached over plain HTTP until the app proxy exists, as in upstream's compose file), `disable-admin-console` (not packaged). Telemetry is off.
- Non-root: Penpot's three containers as UID 1001 (the images' `penpot` user), PostgreSQL as UID 70 (the Alpine image's `postgres` user) and Valkey as UID 999. No privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.
- Volumes: `penpot-data` (20 GiB, assets) and `penpot-db` (20 GiB, the designs).
- Probes: `GET /readyz` on the backend (6060) and exporter (6061); the frontend is ready when the backend is.

## First run

Source: [docs/technical-guide/getting-started/docker.md](https://github.com/penpot/penpot/blob/2.19.1/docs/technical-guide/getting-started/docker.md).

1. Install Penpot from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-penpot`. The first start runs database migrations and can take a few minutes.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:9001 (the address Penpot is configured with):
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-penpot port-forward svc/penpot 9001:9001
   ```
3. Create an account. Registration is open, and email verification is off because no mail server is configured, so create yours right after install and then invite others from a team.

## Not done yet

- No email (SMTP): invitations and password resets are not mailed (upstream's compose file uses a test mail catcher, not packaged).
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the app is reached through a port-forward on port 9001 until the app proxy exists. `PENPOT_PUBLIC_URI` matches that port-forward.
- The backend and exporter listen on all pod addresses (ports 6060 and 6061), not only 127.0.0.1, so another pod on the box could reach them directly until per-app network policies exist.
- The admin console and the MCP server are not packaged.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: the frontend's entrypoint writes its nginx configuration at start.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices below upstream's server guidance (4 CPUs, 16 GB for thousands of users). Idle memory was measured on a k3s smoke test (arm64, 2026-11-12) and the figures were raised to leave headroom above it. They are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212771377, job `gate (penpot)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `docker.io/library/postgres:15.19-trixie`: CVE-2025-68121 in the Go `stdlib` v1.24.6, fixed in 1.24.13, 1.25.7 or 1.26.0-rc.3.
- Secret finding (Trivy): the same postgres image has `private-key` (HIGH) in `/etc/ssl/private/ssl-cert-snakeoil.key` (Debian's ssl-cert package).
- Licence: GitHub MPL-2.0 matches, but there is no research licence-matrix row, so the app is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10).
- Passed: the penpot backend, frontend and exporter 2.19.1 images (no CRITICAL with a fix), valkey, ClamAV (0 infected), smoke test (GET / returned 200).

To unblock: move the pins to upstream releases that fix these findings (tags that exist, checked with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the daily `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag.

**Unblock attempt (apps/market-unblock-2, 2026-11-13):** Only the bundled `postgres:15.19-trixie` blocked this app on images (backend, frontend, exporter, valkey, ClamAV and smoke test passed); the licence-matrix row is still missing (brief 30 B10), which the gate reports as a note about preinstalling on sold boxes. The sidecar moved to `postgres:15.19-alpine` (same major and minor; tag and digest read from the Docker Hub registry on 2026-11-13; digest `sha256:eab009ce…b0372f`). The Alpine image uses `su-exec` (C) instead of the Go helper `gosu` and has no Debian `ssl-cert` package, which is where CVE-2025-68121 and the snakeoil private key came from. It has not been scanned by us yet: the CI gate decides the tier. The Alpine `postgres` user is UID/GID 70 (Debian: 999). Alpine uses musl, so text sorting differs from the Debian image; this is safe only because nobody has installed this app yet.
